chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ismail from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed ten [persons] in connection with wine: one who cultivates it, one who nurtures it, one who presses it, one who drinks it, one who serves it, one who carries it, one to whom it is carried, one who sells it, one who buys it, and one who consumes its price.

key_terms.غَارِسَهَا: One who cultivates/plants the fruit for wine

ai.seo_question: Who are the ten people cursed in Islam regarding wine?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* outlines a comprehensive curse on ten categories of individuals involved in the lifecycle of wine, extending the prohibition beyond mere consumption to include cultivation, storage, and economic transactions. In Shia jurisprudence, this enumeration underscores the concept of *sharikah* (partnership in sin), where each participant shares in the spiritual consequence of the intoxicant. The inclusion of the 'eater of its price' highlights the holistic nature of the impurity, affecting not just the physical act but the entire economic ecosystem surrounding the drink.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 11. It was narrated to me by al-Hussain b. Ahmad from his father from Ahmad b. Ali b. Ismail from Ahmad b. al-Nadhr from ’Amru b. Shimr from Jabir from Abi Ja’far (a.s.)

who said: Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) narrates that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) cursed ten persons in connection with wine viz. one who cultivates the fruit, one who nurtures it, one who prepares wine, one who drinks it, one who serves it, one who sends it, one who orders it, one who sells it, one who buys it and one who makes profit from it.
